biography: William "Wild Bill" Owen burst onto the American racing scene from humble beginnings in rural Mississippi. His family owned a small auto repair shop, where he practically grew up surrounded by engines and the smell of gasoline. He started racing go-karts at the age of 10, displaying a natural talent for speed and an aggressive, almost reckless driving style. A defining moment came at 16 when he won the national karting championship, catching the eye of a local racing team owner who offered him a chance to race in Formula Ford. The transition was tough initially, but his raw talent and relentless determination shone through. Currently, at 22, he's making waves in the Ligier JS P217, proving he's got the mettle to take on the endurance racing world.
drivingStyle: Owen's driving style is characterized by aggressive corner entries and late braking maneuvers. He's known for pushing his car to the absolute limit, sometimes flirting with disaster. Tire management is an area he's actively working on, as his early races were often marred by excessive wear. Under pressure, Owen tends to thrive, often pulling off daring overtakes in the closing laps. His fearlessness and instinctual feel for the car make him a captivating driver to watch.

rivalries.reason: Rossi is a veteran known for his calculated approach, a stark contrast to Owen's wild style. Their clashes on the track are always a battle of experience versus raw talent.
Dubois and Owen have a history of intense battles, often involving close calls and accusations of aggressive driving from both sides.
Tanaka and Owen were both rookies together and frequently fought for position, leading to multiple on-track incidents and a simmering rivalry.

quirks: Always wears a lucky pair of socks with a checkered flag pattern.
Listens to a specific hard rock song on repeat an hour before every race.
Always touches the front left tire of his car three times before getting in.
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans Rookie of the Year award in his debut year after leading for several hours.
careerLowPoint: Spinning out while leading the final lap of a major endurance race, costing his team the victory.
